Goldman Sachs Summer Analyst Internship
Naman Kothari, B.Tech IT 2021-24
Online Test - 13th August 2022
Students from all branches were allowed to sit for the test. The test was on
HackerRank and was divided into four sections. It was a proctored test that required
camera and audio permissions. Changing the tab would lead to being flagged. Each
section had a separate timer which meant that you could not carry forward the time
from any other section and you couldn’t navigate back to a section after submitting it.
4 Sections of Online test :
Coding/Programming Questions : (30 mins)
There were 2 coding questions of moderate difficulty.
Maximum sum square sub-matrix of a given size.
The question was not direct it had a long story. There is a football player who wants to
score a goal in a square sub-region of the ground. The ground is represented by an n*n
2-d matrix where each element is positive and the value at index(i,j) denotes the score
the player gets if the goal is scored at that location. The square region should be of
size k*k. Find the square sub-matrix where the player should score a goal to get the
maximum average score, where the average is calculated by finding the sum of
elements in the square matrix divided by a number of elements in that square matrix.
Based on the constraints given, a brute force solution passed all the test cases here.
The second question was not standard. Again, it was given in the form of a long story.
Given, an array bike where the element at index I, denotes the power of bike[i]. Also, an
array of riders is given, where riders[i] denote the riding capacity of the ith rider. Find
how the bikes should be allocated to the riders so that the product of bike[i]*rider[j] for
every (bike, rider) pair should be greater than a given threshold value. We had to find
all possible combinations.

2
Sample Input :  bike = [3,2,4]      &     rider = [7,3,5]        threshold k= 8 Output: 4
Here, for 3 bikes and 3 riders, there can be 6 different combinations, but out of these,
only 4 combinations will satisfy the given condition.
(bike1,rider1) , (bike2,rider2), (bike3,rider3)  → (3*7=21) , (2*3=6) , (4*5=20)
The wrong combination as 2nd pair has product 6 which is less than 8
(bike1,rider1) , (bike2,rider3) , (bike3,rider2) → (3*7=21) , (2*5=10) , (4*3=12)
The valid combination as all pairs have a product greater than 8.
Similarly, 3 more valid combinations exist.
Aptitude Questions : (45 mins)
12 Maths-based MCQ questions with +5 and -2 marking schemes were given. It had
probability, permutation, and combination, A.P., G.P., matrices, etc. I do not recollect the
questions.
HR Essay Section : (15 mins)
2 questions were given which were HR-based (Limit 200 Words Per Answer)
1) Describe an incident when you felt that your passion helped you achieve a goal.
2) You and your classmate have been working hard on a challenging team project.
You are on track to complete the project on time, but there is still a lot of work to
be done, your classmate has a personal situation that requires him to stop
working on the project. What would you do in this situation?
CS Fundamentals Section : (20 mins)
7 CS-related MCQ questions with +5 and -2 marking schemes. It had OS, OOPs,
DBMS,  CN, and a few debugging/output-related questions. The questions were fairly
easy or moderate, you only needed to worry about the time crunch. Debugging
questions are a bit tricky, so solve them carefully.
The shortlisted candidates were announced 2 days before the interviews. You could
practice questions from here during the period between online assessments and
interviews. Revise all the CS Fundamentals during this phase and go through all the
previously asked questions from different interview experiences.
Also, go through puzzles from here
I collected some questions from the interview experiences of our seniors from CoC and
revised them thoroughly.

3
OnCampus Interviews - 16th August 2022
All interviews are held on the same day. 36 students were shortlisted for the
interviews. The interviews were held offline, on campus. There were 2 or 3 rounds of
interviews all were technical rounds depending on the candidate’s performance.
Round 1: Technical Interview (30 mins)
The interview started with the standard question “Tell me about yourself”. Have some
pointers ready in your mind to answer this question as this part is very important.
Based on your introduction, the interviewer might ask you certain questions.
In my introduction, I highlighted hackathons and social good projects. And as I
expected I was asked some questions on the same. One of my projects was discussed
for about 5-10 mins. I mentioned the purpose of the project, what problems it solved,
some notable features, and highlights of the tech stack used.
Then the interviewer asked me to explain to her a data structure of my choice. This
was an open-ended question so try to add some things which make your answer
special and stand out. I explained stacks using an example of books. Then she asked
me about the different functions of stacks. This time I mentioned push(), pop(), top(),
and I deliberately mentioned getmin() also as a custom function. This played well and
she asked me to explain getmin(). I first told her an approach on how I will maintain a
minimum while pushing and told her the problems that will occur if we use this
method directly then, I mentioned another method. The method I mentioned was this
one. The interviewer seemed very much satisfied with the point that I didn’t do only
the bare minimum as I would have only mentioned standard operations, but I would
suggest you explain complex use cases also for the same.
Another question was about Binary Search Tree. She told me to explain Binary search
Trees first. I gave her a gist on the same and some operations.
Then she came up with this question.
I told her that we would find the inorder traversal of the tree and then find the element
on the kth index according to our requirement. She asked me to write the code for the
same. The first interview concluded here and she told me that we might call you for
another round soon.

4
Key Takeaways from this round:-
Think loud, and always communicate your approach to the interviewer continuously.
For open-ended questions try to tell something extra as the interviewer knows the
bare minimum already. This could prove to be a distinguishing point in such cases. The
interviewer was very friendly and overall the round was easy.
Round 2: Technical Interview (40 mins)
This time the interviewer first enquired about the topics I was asked in the prior round.
Then he asked me that apart from problem-solving which other subjects I like. I
mentioned operating systems. Then he asked me, “Which data structures are you
comfortable with?” This time I played safe and told him that I m familiar with linear
data structures. The conversation went on about databases for some time and he
thoroughly examined my resume. Further, he asked me about MongoDb and NoSql
Databases and also about Cassandra. I answered him that it is an example of NoSql
databases, but I am not familiar with that. I also mentioned some advantages of NoSql
Databases as a response to a previous question.
Then he moved to an open-ended DSA Problem: Merge 2 sorted Arrays (He didn’t
mention anything about space and time but through the discussion, I was able to
conclude that he was interested in space optimization. Though he asked me for the
most optimized solution, I advise you to discuss different approaches as it shows your
thinking process. On every approach, he encouraged me to optimize it more, and finally,
I gave him a very unique method to solve the problem.
I answered a total of 4 different approaches.
Approach 1 - Similar to merge sort
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/merge-two-sorted-arrays/
Approach 2 - 2 Pointer Approach
1) Initialize i,j,k as 0,0,n-1 where n is size of arr1
2) Iterate through every element of arr1 and arr2 using two pointers i and j respectively
if arr1[i] is less than arr2[j]
increment i
else
swap the arr2[j] and arr1[k]

5
increment j and decrement k
3) Sort both arr1 and arr2
Approach 3 - Similar to Insertion Sort involving 2 Pointers
Approach 4 - Gap Method
Both of them can be found here.
After this question, he told me that he was done with his questions and asked me if I
had any questions for him. I enquired about the culture at Goldman Sachs.
Key Takeaways from this round:-
The gap method really worked out for me on this question as it was not all intuitive but
luckily I knew that method and I mentioned it. So, if you encounter any such questions
with multiple approaches in an interview then always discuss multiple approaches for
the same. The interviewer also gave a remark that the purpose of such questions is not
to test whether you can solve it or not but to examine how deeply you can think and
how diversly you can come up with different approaches for a specific problem.
After this round, I was waiting for the third round in the seminar hall as my friends
were called for the subsequent rounds. After some time we were informed that the
interview process is over for the day and the feedback will be informed to the TPO till
evening. I thought that I would not get selected as I did not get a chance for the 3rd
round.
But to my surprise when the list of selected candidates was announced, I was
fortunate enough to be one of them. They selected 2 applicants directly from those
who appeared for the second round, and 6 applicants out of those who appeared for
the third round. In total, 8 of us (5 girls, 3 boys) were offered the internship.

7
Preparation Tips:
It's quite normal to get rejected. Don’t get dejected after rejections. There will be plenty of
opportunities and you just need one.
Prepare the CS Fundamentals well in your 4th semester itself.
Try to make an introduction in such a way that it directs the interview in such a direction in
which you are interested and will be comfortable answering.
Whenever you are preparing for an interview, reading company-specific archives and interview
experiences helps a lot. You will get a basic idea of what kind of questions you will be asked
and what their domain can be. Different questions about your projects can also be asked.
Lastly, it’s okay to be nervous. It’s okay to not stay calm. But don’t let it affect your interview.
Be confident about yourself, and everything shall go well.
All the Best!
